newsitem.title: INDIA: Indian sugar prices fall on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Indian sugar prices fall on profit-taking.

text.p: Indian sugar prices fell on Tuesday on low consumer demand and profit-taking, dealers said.
They said unconfirmed reports that the government had postponed plans to raise the price of sugar sold through state-sponsored shops helped bolster prices.

"The market was firm during last week on expectations the government may hike selling prices of sugar supplied through the public distribution system by more than 100 rupees per quintal," said Shantilal Dedhiya, secretary of Bombay Sugar Merchant's Association.
In the ready delivery sugar, S-30 fell by 10 rupees to 1,240/1,265 rupees per quintal while M-30 slid by same margin at 1,275/1,350 rupees per quintal.
Sugar mill delivery however remained untraded as most of the delivery tenders out of the free sale quota for current month are exhausted.
